issue.description:
Split child of beadrs-8923aef3; depends on beadrs-3ade3e50 (multi-generation round trip). Redaction rewrites historical events in place, so it is one of the two paths that could silently drop unknown fields. Add/verify a conformance test that redacts an event carrying unknown extensions, re-publishes the generation, and asserts the unknown fields on that event survive the rewrite (subject to the documented redaction-marker semantics — a redacted payload value is replaced, but unrelated extension keys on the event record must persist into the next generation).
Acceptance criteria:
- An extension-bearing event is redacted on a real store (not a hand-built fixture only).
- The next published generation still carries the event's unknown extension keys, with the marker semantics asserted explicitly.
- Suite green locally; evidence recorded on this bead.
issue.notes: Verified attempt 1's already-committed test (94490ae) against the acceptance criteria and spec: assertions match historical-redaction-v1 section 3 exactly (only the finding byte range is replaced with [REDACTED:bead-rs]; unrelated fields MUST remain unchanged). The redaction runs on a real store via the CLI on the round-tripped workspace, generation 4 re-publishes, assert_levels_preserved pins the event's extension keys (future_tier plus the replay widening) parse-equal on the rewritten event itself, the rewritten detail must parse-equal {credential: marker}, and the secret bytes must appear nowhere in the published generation. No further source changes were needed. Full DoD (fmt + clippy + test) passed in a clean git-archive extraction of the pushed tree, exit 0; the acceptance suite passed 3/3 there too. Pushed to origin, upstream current (a background checkpoint publish 02162c5 landed on top after verification; source tree identical to the verified extraction).
issue.title: Add redaction-path conformance for unknown fields on rewritten events

issue.description:
Observed 2026-10-03 switching commitgraph to sharded mode (bead sync configure, f3dc595): forensic.jsonl stays on disk as the last monolith and is never updated again. Plan 6.1.1 calls it the nonauthoritative view 'of an active forensic monolith' and publication deliberately never tombstones it (is_generation_object_path excludes it), so after a monolithic->sharded transition it is stale data with no monolith behind it. The environment's documented recovery (/home/coding/CLAUDE.md 'Recovering a broken or fresh-clone workspace': bead sync import-only --input .beads/checkpoint/forensic.jsonl --restore-into-empty) would then silently restore old state.
Decided here: a generation published in sharded mode removes the compatibility view (record it in the changed-path set as a deletion; git tracks the removal), and a later transition back to monolithic recreates it. Update plan 6.1.1/6.2 to say the view exists only while the active generation is monolithic.
Acceptance: test - monolithic workspace with a view, configure --mode sharded, view gone and listed in the generation's changed/deleted paths; back to monolithic, view byte-identical to the root; sync status ready_to_commit; doctor clean.
